reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need a function that maps any real input to a smooth value between 0 and 1. The logistic function provides this by taking any number and feeding it into an exponential denominator. As the input grows very large or very small, the output smoothly saturates at the limits of one and zero.

To understand how this squeezing works, we examine the logistic curve $y = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (x - x0)))$. The parameter $k$ controls the steepness of the transition, while $x0$ shifts the center point horizontally. By observing the curve and its tangent slope at various marker positions, we can see exactly how rapid changes are compressed into a bounded range.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any input into $0$ to $1$. Adjust the steepness, midpoint, and marker to inspect the curve and its slope.
reply.instructions: Adjust the sliders to change steepness, midpoint, and marker position. Observe how the output and slope respond.
